## Investment Thesis
Bitfarms is a publicly-traded Bitcoin miner operating in Canada and internationally. Revenue growth of 72% reflects both rising BTC prices and ongoing hashrate expansion. However, the company is loss-making on a GAAP basis (PE=0, negative forward PE), suggesting that even at $90K+ BTC prices, BITF is not generating meaningful net income — a red flag for operational efficiency.

The share count discrepancy (API 401M vs mktcap-implied 605.9M) is significant — suggesting a fully-diluted count that includes unexercised warrants and convertibles typical of BTC mining capital structures. Using the correct 605.9M diluted count reduces per-share economics substantially.

BTC mining economics are inherently cyclical. At BTC cycle peaks, miners report high TTM revenue; at troughs, miners trade near zero. Our through-cycle normalization applies mean-reversion: bear case assumes BTC corrects to $30K (2022-level), compressing margins to 5%; base case holds $70-90K with 12% through-cycle margin; bull case assumes $150K+ BTC with 25% margins.

The SELL rating reflects that at $1.98, BITF is modestly above intrinsic value even under a favorable BTC scenario. The marginal -18.2% downside makes this a weaker conviction SELL vs CIFR or CLSK, but the risk/reward is unfavorable given commodity mining exposure and share count dilution.
